1. The Principle of Mutual Covenant (Al-Uqud) in Islam

In Islamic jurisprudence, every agreement between two consenting parties is governed by the divine command in Surah Al-Ma’idah (5:1): “O you who have believed, fulfill all contractual obligations (*Awfu bil-Uqud*).” By accessing, browsing, bookmarking, or utilizing the computational tools and written articles on Namaz-e-Shariq, you signify your full acknowledgment and acceptance of the terms, conditions, and disclaimers detailed within this agreement.

If you do not concur with any part of these terms or our methodological guidelines, we respectfully ask that you refrain from relying upon these digital calculations for your religious obligations and consult directly with your local mosque imams and certified Islamic authorities in your physical geographic locality.

2. Astronomical Nature of Calculations & Necessary Precaution (Ihtiyat)

The daily prayer times presented across our city directories (including Bangalore, Delhi, Mumbai, Karachi, Lahore, Dhaka, Dubai, Sharjah, London, New York, and all affiliated hubs) are computed mathematically utilizing rigorous spherical solar coordinate algorithms. These algorithms evaluate the Julian date, solar declination, and equation of time relative to the observer’s geographic latitude and longitude.

While mathematical formulas provide remarkable theoretical precision, the physical observation of the sun and twilight is subject to dynamic terrestrial factors that cannot always be fully captured by digital computation alone:

  • Optical Atmospheric Refraction: Variations in temperature, atmospheric pressure, and coastal humidity can alter the apparent altitude of the sun near the horizon by several arcminutes.
  • Topographical Elevation: Observers located on elevated plateaus (such as Bangalore at ~920m above sea level) or upper floors of high-rise residential towers in Dubai or Karachi observe sunrise earlier and sunset later than ground-level sea horizons.
  • Horizon Obstructions & Light Pollution: Dense urban skylines, mountainous terrain, or high ambient artificial lighting can delay the unaided human eye’s detection of true dawn (*Subh Sadiq*).
The Golden Rule of Sunnah Precaution (Ihtiyat):

In accordance with classical Fiqh manuals across all four Sunni madhhabs, worshipers are strongly encouraged to observe a safety margin:

  • Sehri (Fasting Cutoff): Stop eating and drinking 4 to 5 minutes prior to the calculated Subh Sadiq time.
  • Maghrib (Iftar): Allow a 2 to 3 minute margin after calculated sunset before breaking fast or praying to ensure total disappearance of the solar disk.
  • Prohibited Times: Avoid all prayers during the 15-20 minutes following sunrise and the 5-7 minutes of solar zenith (*Zawal*) before Dhuhr.

3. Primacy of the Local Mosque Congregation (Jamat)

Namaz-e-Shariq provides Awwal Waqt (the exact astronomical beginning and expiration boundaries of each prayer window). However, local mosques (*Masajid*) deliberately schedule their congregational assembly times (*Jamat*) roughly 15 to 45 minutes after the entry of waqt to permit the neighborhood community to perform ablution (*Wudu*) and assemble in rows.

Believers must always give precedence to the congregational schedule of their local mosque when praying with the community. Offering congregational Salah in union with your local community carries twenty-seven times the reward of praying in isolation, and minor schedule variations between neighboring mosques are a natural expression of communal facilitation permitted in the Sunnah.

4. Juristic Differences (Ikhtilaf) & Multi-School Inclusivity

Our platform explicitly facilitates calculations conforming to both the Hanafi school (Asr shadow factor 2, as widely observed across Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Turkey, and Central Asia) and the Shafi’i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools (Asr shadow factor 1, as observed across Kerala, coastal Karnataka, Egypt, Southeast Asia, and the Arabian Peninsula).

We honor legitimate scholarly differences (*Ikhtilaf*) as an authentic mercy within Islamic legal history. Users can toggle freely between calculation methods and schools within our live widget. The editorial board does not endorse sectarian exclusivism and provides verified citations for all presented rulings.
